_note: English trade taxonomy. Slugs are shared across all languages so a URL keeps working when the visitor switches language. German levels and recognition rules are indicative and vary by Land and employer — the trade page says so. `salaryBand` stays null until a verifiable source is validated.

trades.label: Nurse
trades.summary: Germany is recruiting heavily in care. The profession is regulated: your diploma has to be recognised, and a solid level of German is required before you start.
requirements: State nursing diploma, with training transcripts
German level usually required: B2
Diploma recognition procedure (Anerkennung) to be started
Clinical experience valued, especially in a specialist unit
dossier: Language certificate if you have one
CV detailing the units and procedures

trades.label: Care assistant
trades.summary: German care homes and clinics recruit continuously. The language requirements are more accessible than for a registered nurse post.
requirements: Care assistant training or demonstrable equivalent experience
German level usually asked for: B1
Recognition of the training advisable depending on the Land
Availability for shift work
dossier: CV listing the types of facility

trades.label: Electrician
trades.summary: Permanently in short supply across German construction and industry. Hands-on practice counts as much as the diploma.
requirements: Vocational training in electrical work or equivalent experience
German level usually asked for: B1 (workplace safety)
Electrical authorisations appreciated
Able to read plans and wiring diagrams
dossier: CV listing the types of site

trades.label: Welder
trades.summary: German industry recruits qualified welders. It is one of the trades where the language bar is lowest at the start.
requirements: Command of at least one process (TIG, MIG/MAG, stick)
German often accepted from A2, to be improved afterwards
Welding certifications valued
Able to read technical drawings

trades.label: Industrial mechanic
trades.summary: Maintenance and production: durable positions across a dense network of German SMEs that are actively short-staffed.
requirements: Training in mechanics, maintenance or machining
German level usually asked for: B1
Experience on machine tools or production lines
Able to read plans and technical documentation

trades.label: Cook
trades.summary: German hotels and restaurants recruit all year round, with moderate language requirements on hiring.
requirements: Culinary training or experience in an establishment
German often accepted from A2
Knowledge of hygiene standards
Availability for split shifts and weekends
dossier: CV listing venue types and covers

trades.label: HGV driver
trades.summary: German road haulage is short of drivers. The licence and the professional qualification have to be converted.
requirements: Valid heavy goods vehicle licence
Professional driver qualification to be recognised
German level usually asked for: B1
Long-distance experience appreciated
dossier: CV listing vehicle types and routes

trades.label: Software developer
trades.summary: The trade where English most often suffices to start: many German teams work in English day to day.
requirements: Demonstrable technical skills (projects, code repositories)
German B1 appreciated; professional English is often enough
A degree is not systematically required
Team and agile experience valued
dossier: Links to your projects or code
